html:
On 29 May 1919 the British astronomer Arthur Eddington photographed a total eclipse of the sun from a cocoa estate on Príncipe, to test whether the sun's gravity bends starlight.

A second team observed the same eclipse from Sobral in Brazil. Their plates showed the stars shifted by about the amount Einstein's general theory of relativity predicted, rather than the smaller amount from Newton's physics. When the result was announced in London in November 1919, Einstein became famous around the world overnight.

Eddington worked at Roça Sundy, one of the great estates of the cocoa era. A plaque there marks the site, and the island celebrated the centenary in 2019. It ties a small colony to a turning point in physics.
